posts.title: Welcome to Vesper — A New Era of Minecraft Launching
posts.author: ItzzMateo
posts.excerpt: Introducing Vesper: a Minecraft launcher built from scratch with Rust + GPUI for instant startup and a modern native experience.
posts.content:
## Why Vesper?

The Minecraft launcher space has been dominated by heavy Electron and Java-based solutions for years. They eat up your RAM, take forever to start, and feel outdated.

**Vesper** changes that. Built from scratch with **Rust** and **GPUI**, we're creating a launcher that starts in milliseconds, uses minimal resources, and looks beautiful doing it.

## What Makes Us Different

- **Sub-second startup** — No more waiting 10+ seconds for a launcher to load
- **Minimal RAM usage** — Written in Rust, not Electron
- **Native UI** — GPUI renders a buttery smooth interface
- **Free & open source** — Always will be

## Our Vision

We believe launching Minecraft should be as fast and enjoyable as playing it. Vesper is our answer to the bloat.

## Get Involved

Vesper is currently in alpha. Join our Discord at **[dc.devflare.de](https://dc.devflare.de)** to apply for early access and help shape the product.

posts.title: Why We Chose Rust + GPUI Over Electron
posts.author: ItzzMateo
posts.excerpt: A deep dive into our technology choices and why Rust + GPUI is the future of desktop applications.
posts.content:
## The Problem with Electron

Electron bundles a full Chromium browser with your app. The result? A "hello world" app that uses 100MB+ of RAM and takes seconds to start.

For a Minecraft launcher — something you open every time you play — this overhead adds up fast.

## Enter Rust

Rust gives us:

- **Memory safety** without garbage collection
- **Blazing fast** compile times and runtime performance
- **Small binary sizes** — our entire launcher is under 10MB

## Why GPUI?

GPUI is a GPU-accelerated UI framework that renders interfaces directly on the GPU. No browser, no DOM, no overhead.

The result is a launcher that feels **instant** — menus open in milliseconds, scrolling is buttery smooth, and animations run at 60fps without breaking a sweat.

## Benchmarks

| Metric | Vesper | Electron Launcher |
|--------|--------|-------------------|
| Startup time | ~0.3s | ~4.2s |
| RAM usage | ~45MB | ~350MB |
| Binary size | ~8MB | ~150MB |

These numbers speak for themselves.

## Looking Forward

As GPUI matures, we'll continue pushing the boundaries of what a desktop launcher can be. Stay tuned.

posts.title: Alpha Testing Guide — What to Expect
posts.author: ItzzMateo
posts.excerpt: Everything you need to know about Vesper's alpha program, how to apply, and what we expect from testers.
posts.content:
## Alpha Program Overview

Vesper is currently in **alpha testing**. This means the core features are working, but there will be bugs, missing features, and rough edges.

## How to Apply

1. Join our Discord at **[dc.devflare.de](https://dc.devflare.de)**
2. Head to the **#alpha-application** channel
3. Tell us about your Minecraft setup and what you'd like to see in a launcher

We prioritize applicants who:

- Play Minecraft regularly
- Have experience with different launchers
- Are willing to provide detailed feedback
- Can test on different operating systems

## What We Expect

- **Report bugs** — Even small ones help us improve
- **Suggest features** — Your ideas shape the product
- **Be patient** — Alpha software has rough edges
- **Have fun** — This is a passion project for all of us

## What You'll Get

- Early access to all features before public release
- Direct communication with the dev team
- Your name in the contributors list
- A warm fuzzy feeling from helping build something great

## Current Status

- Core launcher functionality: ✅ Working
- Mod support: 🚧 In progress
- Custom themes: 📋 Planned
- Multi-instance: 📋 Planned

We're making rapid progress. Apply today and be part of the journey!

posts.title: Performance Deep Dive — How We Achieved Sub-Second Startup
posts.author: ItzzMateo
posts.excerpt: A technical deep dive into the architecture decisions that make Vesper launch in under 300ms.
posts.content:
## The Goal

We set an ambitious target: **sub-second startup**. Not just "fast for a launcher" — genuinely instant.

## Architecture Decisions

### No Runtime Dependencies

Vesper is a single statically-linked binary. No Node.js, no Python, no Java — just one file you double-click and it runs.

### Lazy Loading

We only load what's needed for the current view. The mod manager, settings panel, and other features load on demand — not at startup.

### GPU-Accelerated Rendering

GPUI handles all rendering on the GPU. No CPU-based layout calculations, no DOM diffing — just raw GPU power.

### Efficient State Management

Our state management is built on Rust's ownership model. No unnecessary re-renders, no memory leaks, no garbage collection pauses.

## Results

On our test machines:

- **Cold start**: 280ms
- **Warm start**: 90ms
- **Memory idle**: 42MB
- **Memory with mods loaded**: 78MB

These are real numbers from real hardware, not synthetic benchmarks.

## What's Next

We're still optimizing. Our target is **under 100ms** cold start by the time we hit public beta.
